1.why: All screens use a clean sans-serif typeface with comfortable line spacing in instruction text, though letter spacing appears standard rather than generous.

2.why: Instructional text on every step is sentence case, non-italic, and broken into one- or two-sentence blocks; only the brand wordmark 'NORTHSTAR BANK' is all-caps.

3.why: Every screenshot shows a single narrow column with large fields and full-width buttons that fits a mobile viewport without crowding.

4.why: Instructions are one to two short sentences and mostly plain, but terms like 'provisioning value' and 'provisioning representation' are technical jargon.

5.why: The recovery code field shows a format example 'ABCD-EFGH-JKLM' and demo credentials are given, but the verification code and authenticator code fields show no example of the expected input.

6.why: No screen contains more than a two-sentence instruction block; all content needed to proceed is brief.

7.why: The manual secret, otpauth URI, and recovery codes are rendered as selectable text that can be copied, though no dedicated copy button is provided.

8.why: No QR code image is displayed on the authenticator setup step; only a raw otpauth:// text URI is shown despite the instruction telling the user to 'scan the provisioning value.'

9.why: Standard labelled text and password inputs are used, but no autofill or password-manager behaviour can be confirmed from the screenshots.

10.why: Each page has a clear bold heading naming the step and a prominent dark-green primary button, though there is no explicit step-of-total progress indicator.

11.why: Most screens present a single primary action, but the Recovery codes screen asks the user to choose between 'Use recovery code' and 'Generate replacement recovery codes.'

12.why: Successful actions are confirmed plainly (e.g., 'MFA is enabled'), but failed sign-ins produce repeated vague 'Unable to continue sign-in.' banners with no statement of what happened or what comes next.

13.why: The user retried sign-in many times and regenerated recovery codes with no lockout or penalty, though no reveal/hide control for the password field is offered.

14.why: Errors are non-blaming but unhelpful: 'Unable to continue sign-in.' states neither the problem nor the fix, and one error is raw developer jargon ('Failed to execute insertBefore on Node').

15.why: No reading countdown is shown, but the verification code is described as 'short-lived' and authenticator codes 'rotate every 30 seconds,' imposing real time pressure on code entry.
